classification_basis: largest contiguous usable foundation-equivalent core at a sampled horizontal platform elevation; total connected area is secondary

small.intent: local or satellite production; limited expansion

medium.intent: dedicated factory with meaningful miner/belt upgrade headroom

large.intent: major production district intended to survive multiple throughput upgrades

very_large.intent: regional or late-game industrial campus where terrain should not be the primary growth constraint

workable.interpretation: usable for most factories with some layout constraint

linear.interpretation: long/narrow surface; potentially useful for linear production but not general-purpose

poor.interpretation: too elongated to treat raw area as equivalent general-purpose industrial capacity

notes: Horizontal resolution and vertical step are independent. Resolution controls boundary/detail fidelity; step controls which horizontal platform elevations are sampled.

Each coarse horizontal cell is obstructed until the platform plane reaches the maximum terrain elevation within that cell. This preserves small ridges at coarse resolution instead of erasing them with a median.
Water is treated as a temporary height obstruction by default: a cell with water becomes available once the platform plane rises above the water surface. It is not permanently excluded.
At a fixed platform elevation, changing vertical step does not change geometry; step only changes the sampled elevations included in a run.
Usable area is monotonic with platform elevation: higher planes can add or merge cells but cannot remove previously usable cells.
Grade, roughness and confidence remain diagnostics unless explicit gates are configured.
Size thresholds remain parameterized calibration defaults and are expected to change after in-game validation.
build_surfaces_v1.json and build_surfaces_v2.json are retained as historical policies for reproducibility.
